PathwayNurse.dc.html: Regulator: the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO). Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a registered nurse in Ontario until the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO) registers you.
Apply to CNO online and pay the fee. Allow about 15 days for a first update.
CNO checks your nursing education against the RN baccalaureate standard; you may need a Transition to Practice course.
Not a graduate in the last 3 years? Show evidence of recent practice.
Pass the NCLEX-RN when CNO says you can register for it.
Show English or French language proficiency, your right to work, a declaration of past offences and a police check.

PathwayPhysician.dc.html: Regulator: CPSO. Routes differ a lot by where you trained — this shows the main ones. Settle never decides which route applies.
You can't work as a physician in Ontario until the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) registers you.
A route set by Ontario regulation or a CPSO policy
Read CPSO's registration requirements and pick the route that fits your training.

Some routes: the Royal College Practice Eligibility Route (supervised restricted certificate up to 3 years), Subspecialist Affiliate status, or CFPC certification without exam for family doctors from Australia, Ireland, the UK and the US.
Apply online through CPSO's portal — CPSO assesses credentials itself.
You don't need PR for a certificate, but you need a valid work permit or status to work.

PathwayPharmacist.dc.html: Regulator: the Ontario College of Pharmacists (OCP). Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a pharmacist in Ontario until the Ontario College of Pharmacists (OCP) registers you.
Create a Pharmacists' Gateway Canada account (NAPRA) and pay the enrolment fee.
Pass or be exempted from the PEBC Evaluating Exam, then choose Ontario.
Pass the PEBC Qualifying Exam and show language proficiency.
Register as an intern: liability insurance, police check, fee.
Pass the jurisprudence exam and complete PACE during your intern year.
Until you're registered as an intern, you can't practise pharmacy in Ontario — even under supervision. The full process takes about 5–18 months.

PathwayDentist.dc.html: Regulator: the Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario (RCDSO). Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a dentist in Ontario until the Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario (RCDSO) registers you.
Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario
NDEB Equivalency Process or a degree completion program
From each regulator you were licensed with
Check if your dental program is accredited (CDAC, CODA, or listed Australian, New Zealand or Irish programs).
Accredited: go straight to NDEB Certification.
Not accredited: pass the NDEB Equivalency Process (three exams), or complete a qualifying program (U of T IDAPP or Western's Advanced Standing Program).
Complete NDEB Certification, including the Virtual OSCE.
Apply to RCDSO with a Certificate of Standing from every past regulator.

PathwayTeacher.dc.html: Regulator: the Ontario College of Teachers (OCT). Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a teacher (k–12) in Ontario until the Ontario College of Teachers (OCT) registers you.
Check you have a 3-year postsecondary degree and a four-semester teacher education program.
Attend an OCT information session for internationally educated teachers.
Get your academic records and statement of professional standing — the rules depend on your country.
Apply online when you have every document and can pay the fees; your application is valid for one year.
Meet the language requirement if you trained in another language.
Complete the Sexual Abuse Prevention Program and a criminal record check.

PathwayECE.dc.html: Early childhood educator: your licensing pathway
Regulator: the College of Early Childhood Educators. Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a early childhood educator in Ontario until the College of Early Childhood Educators registers you.
If you studied in another language
Check you have a four-semester ECE diploma or degree.
Order a WES ICAP document-by-document report; WES sends it and your transcripts to the College.
Send course outlines from your school, translated into English or French if needed.
If you studied in another language, send a test score (e.g. IELTS 6.5 in each band, CELPIP 8).
Pay the non-refundable application fee. Files are reviewed only once complete.
Not approved? You can ask for a review within 60 days.

PathwayLawyer.dc.html: Regulator: the Law Society of Ontario (LSO). Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a lawyer in Ontario until the Law Society of Ontario (LSO) registers you.
Federation of Law Societies' National Committee on Accreditation
Apply to the NCA for an assessment of your law degree.
Complete the subjects it lists (usually 6–9) through NCA exams or Canadian law school courses.
Receive your NCA Certificate of Qualification.
Register with the LSO licensing process early; complete its exams and experiential training (articling interviews usually happen the summer before).

PathwayCPA.dc.html: Regulator: CPA Ontario. The title "CPA" is protected; most accounting jobs don't need the public accounting licence.
You can't work as a accountant (cpa) in Ontario until CPA Ontario registers you.
Check whether your accounting body has an agreement with CPA Ontario (e.g. US state boards, IMCP Mexico, ICAEW, CAANZ, HKICPA, CA Ireland, ICAS, SAICA, ICAI India, ICAP Pakistan, ICAN Nigeria, CIMA).
Follow the route for your body: mutual recognition, reciprocal membership, recognized body or the express MOU route.
No agreement? Apply for advance standing in the CPA student program.
For public accounting, complete CPARE and apply for the licence.

PathwayElectrician.dc.html: Regulator: Skilled Trades Ontario. Steps follow the regulator's own pages — Settle never applies for you or decides if you qualify.
You can't work as a electrician in Ontario until Skilled Trades Ontario registers you.
Fill out the Trade Equivalency Assessment application with the application guide.
Send verifiable evidence that your experience equals the full apprenticeship (on-the-job and in-school hours).
If approved, write the certifying exam.
Pass and pay the fee for your Certificate of Qualification.
Not approved? Ask for a reassessment ($100 + HST) with new evidence.
You need a Certificate of Qualification, a provisional certificate or a registered apprenticeship to work as an electrician in Ontario.
